_note: Newest first. Dates are when the change landed in the development build. Plain wording for people who print, not for developers.

entries.title: Open files into the running app
entries.text: Launch Breadslicer with several model files and they arrive in one scene, each with its file name. With the app already open, new files go to the window you used last instead of starting a second copy.

entries.title: Copy and paste keeps your prep
entries.text: A pasted object brings its hollow and drains, its own editable supports with your hand edits, and its height. One undo takes it all back.

entries.title: Add braces by hand
entries.text: A new Brace tool (C) joins two supports with two clicks, with a green or red preview that says why. Remove takes out a single brace, and every brace is one undo.

entries.title: World and model size side by side
entries.text: When a model is tilted, the Size card shows its size in the world next to its own size. Both can be edited.

entries.title: The first click on an imported model is instant
entries.text: Everything needed to pick a model with the mouse is now prepared while the file loads, so the first click no longer stalls on big miniatures.

entries.title: The start screen comes back on an empty scene
entries.text: Delete the last object or close the scene and the start screen returns, with your recent files. Ctrl+Z brings everything back.

entries.title: Fix all works in the background
entries.text: Fix all no longer freezes the window on scenes with hundreds of findings. It shows its progress and can be cancelled; the result is the same as before.

entries.title: A repair report you can read
entries.text: The Repair report opens with every detail shown, in larger text, and the card grows to fit what it says.

entries.title: Importing several files at once
entries.text: Drop four models and they arrive together, read in parallel, instead of one first and the rest a second later.

entries.title: Generate supports for every selected model
entries.text: With several models selected, Generate makes one set per model, with progress, in a single undo step. A new option lifts models that sit on the plate by 5 mm first.

entries.title: Import adds to the scene
entries.text: File › Import model (Ctrl+I), drag and drop, and the start screen now add models to the current scene, placed in free space without moving anything. Opening a .bread project still replaces the scene.

entries.title: New message cards
entries.text: Every message card now shares the start screen's look: a clear header, a close button and the buttons in the footer.

entries.title: Manual supports: move tips, remove many at once
entries.text: A new Move tip tool (M) drags a support's tip across the surface with a live green or red preview. Remove now works with a box or a brush, and only touches supports you can actually see.

entries.title: A start screen
entries.text: Reopen your last project, open a project, import a model or start empty, with your 10 recent files. It can be turned off in Preferences.

entries.title: Manual supports that attach where you click
entries.text: A hand-placed support hooks onto nearby trunks, Shift+click forces one, keys 1 to 4 pick the tip size, and the preview says why a support cannot attach. A support that needs its own trunk gets bracing to its neighbour.

entries.title: Transform, Supports and Slice in Spanish
entries.text: The rest of the main panels are translated.

entries.title: Filled cavities print without a seam
entries.text: A cavity filled from the review now covers its border pixels too, so no thin line is left where it meets the model.

entries.title: Fill bed
entries.text: Fill the free space of the plate with copies of the selected model, or a fair mix of several. Copies share their mesh, keep their own supports, and the rest of the plate stays where it is.

entries.title: Drains with depth, cones and plugs
entries.text: Drain holes take a fixed or automatic depth, can be cone-shaped, and can come with a matching plug placed next to the model.

entries.title: Presets by model size
entries.text: Two new support presets, for miniatures from 30 mm and figures from 70 mm, size tips, trunks and bracing by zone.

entries.title: Repair shows what it did, and can be cancelled
entries.text: Progress per object, a Cancel that leaves the scene untouched, and red or amber marks on whatever could not be fixed.

entries.title: Paste is instant
entries.text: Pasting a copy of a large model takes about 3 ms, and undoing it about 0.1 ms.

entries.title: Faster start
entries.text: The window appears sooner, on the first launch and on every one after.

entries.title: Closer print time estimates
entries.text: Anycubic printers that use the ZIP file now get a time estimate within a few percent of the real print.

entries.title: Gizmo, second round
entries.text: Plane handles to move on two axes, press and drag any model to move it, a focused gizmo style and a gizmo size setting in Preferences, and R R / S S to turn or scale each selected object around its own centre.

entries.title: A new gizmo
entries.text: Clear outlines and axis colours, live numbers while you drag, a dashed path when moving and a slice when rotating. Ctrl snaps, Shift moves finely.

entries.title: Multi-select
entries.text: Shift+click and Shift+drag a box to select several models. Move, rotate, scale, delete and arrange them together, in one undo step.

entries.title: Orbit around what matters
entries.text: The camera orbits around the selection or the point under the cursor, and the numeric keypad turns the view in 15° steps.

entries.title: Prints on the Photon Mono M7 Pro finish cleanly
entries.text: The Anycubic ZIP file now ends the way the printer expects, so the print no longer stalls on its last layer.

entries.title: Repair that makes broken models printable
entries.text: Repair now welds cracks, separates parts that touch on an edge, orients every piece and closes holes. Every broken model of our test set slices after it.

entries.title: Auto-orient
entries.text: Quick and Full searches for a pose with fewer supports and less peel force, with a live preview and a single undo.

entries.title: The hollow is exactly the preview
entries.text: The cavity you see is the cavity you get: the preview and the result are the same mesh, with the wall measured exactly.

entries.title: Drains cut through infill
entries.text: A drain hole removes every infill pillar or lattice bar it touches, so nothing is left floating inside the channel.

entries.title: Split into bodies
entries.text: Pull a model apart into its separate bodies, or keep only one of them.

entries.title: More files open
entries.text: Duplicate faces are dropped on import, and 3MF files from other tools with untyped parts open.

entries.title: Overlapping parts print
entries.text: Parts that overlap inside one model are no longer dropped from the layers.

entries.title: Resin scale compensation is applied
entries.text: The X/Y/Z compensation in a resin profile now scales the model, its supports and the raft.

entries.title: Files land where you put the model
entries.text: Printer files were rotated half a turn on the plate. Now the model prints where it sits in the app.

entries.title: A much faster viewport
entries.text: The viewport no longer walks every vertex on every frame: a heavy scene went from 55 to 446 frames per second on our machine.

entries.title: Autosave and recovery
entries.text: Unsaved work is kept in the background every 2 minutes and offered back after a crash. Saving over a project keeps its previous versions.

entries.title: Export diagnostics
entries.text: Help › Export Diagnostics saves a .zip you can attach to a bug report, with your user name and folders removed. An optional diagnostic log records the session until you close the app.

entries.title: Arrange all
entries.text: Packs models by their real shape at every height, 1 mm apart, in one undo step.

entries.title: 157 printers
entries.text: The printer list now covers 20 brands, with panels, mirroring and build heights checked against an open-source reference.

entries.title: Supports follow their model
entries.text: Each model has its own supports and raft. Moving or turning a model carries its supports along; tilting or scaling it regenerates them.
